skill.summary: A public reference guide for German e-invoicing readiness, format selection, and archiving documentation.
skill.author: nexaiguy

content.value_statement: German businesses must navigate structured invoice formats, transition dates, and archiving requirements. This public guide helps AI assistants organize readiness questions and draft documentation outlines.
actual_capabilities: Explain the guide's sample turnover-based German B2B transition timeline.
Frame XRechnung and ZUGFeRD selection questions for B2B and B2G scenarios.
Structure readiness checklist drafts around turnover and customer mix.
Guide procedure documentation outline requests for digital invoice workflows.
Identify UStG field mapping and invoice retention as review topics.
limitations: Contains one Markdown guide; scripts, extension source, and original package templates are not included.
Provides no executable XML validator or detailed field mapping tables.
Does not provide legal or tax advice; verify dates, exceptions, and retention rules against current official sources.
Does not cover core Peppol network mechanics or non-German mandates.

use_cases.title: Prepare an SME readiness review
use_cases.description: Organize questions about turnover, customer types, receipt capability, and issuance planning before a professional compliance review.

use_cases.title: Scope invoice format requirements
use_cases.description: Identify recipient requirements and format decisions for a German invoicing integration, while separating guidance from technical validation.

use_cases.title: Draft invoice procedure documentation
use_cases.description: Create an initial workflow outline for receipt, checks, archiving, and retrieval, with unresolved compliance questions marked.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize this guide's German e-invoicing scope in plain language. Separate its stated guidance from rules requiring current official verification.

prompt_templates.title: Build a readiness checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a readiness checklist for a German company with [turnover] annual turnover and [customer mix]. Ask about missing facts and flag deadline assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare format options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare XRechnung and ZUGFeRD for [B2B or B2G scenario]. Identify recipient requirements, routing questions, and validation steps without claiming the guide validates XML.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a procedure review package
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a procedure documentation outline for [invoice workflow]. Include field mapping questions, archiving controls, retention assumptions, and unresolved items for tax and technical reviewers.

output_examples.input: Our German company had EUR 1.2 million turnover last year. What does this guide suggest for domestic B2B invoices?
output: The guide's example states receipt readiness from January 2025 and issuance from January 2027 for turnover above EUR 800,000.
It suggests ZUGFeRD EN 16931 for combined XML and human-readable PDF delivery.
Verify the applicable turnover year, exceptions, recipient requirements, and current official rules before adopting these dates.

output_examples.input: Draft an initial procedure documentation outline for our digital invoice process.
output: Receipt: record channels, responsible staff, and the handling of structured invoice files.
Review: document invoice checks, exceptions, approvals, and required technical validation.
Archiving: describe original-file preservation, access controls, retrieval, and the retention policy.
Open questions: confirm applicable legal requirements and retention periods with the responsible tax adviser.

best_practices: Provide turnover, the relevant financial year, customer locations, and B2B or B2G status before requesting a readiness assessment.
Verify legal dates, exemptions, format versions, and retention rules using current official sources.
Use dedicated invoice validators and obtain professional review before treating generated documentation as compliant.
anti_patterns: Treating the guide's legal currency claims as independent verification or legal advice.
Assuming the public guide includes the paid package's scripts, templates, or automated validation.
Applying one format recommendation to every recipient or extending German guidance to other countries.

faq.question: What is included in this skill?
faq.answer: A public Markdown guide covers German e-invoicing topics and provides an example. Original package scripts, extension source, and templates are absent.

faq.question: Does it validate invoice XML?
faq.answer: No executable validator is included. The guide identifies mandatory field checks as a use case, but technical validation requires separate tooling.

faq.question: Does it provide legal or tax advice?
faq.answer: No. Treat responses as planning drafts and confirm applicable requirements with current official sources and qualified advisers.

faq.question: Does it address both B2B and B2G invoices?
faq.answer: The guide discusses both contexts, including XRechnung, ZUGFeRD, and Leitweg-ID requirements. Confirm the recipient's accepted formats and routing requirements.

faq.question: Does it cover e-invoicing outside Germany?
faq.answer: No. The guide focuses on German requirements and does not cover other national mandates or core Peppol network mechanics.

faq.question: Are its legal dates automatically updated?
faq.answer: No update mechanism is included. The guide claims June 2026 legal coverage; verify current rules and exceptions independently.
